children: Dell Technologies Inc. (DELL, Financials) just added a lot larger figure to the AI infrastructure explosion. Dell finished its fiscal second quarter with a record $95 billion backlog for AI servers after booking $60.9 billion in orders during the period.

The company said revenue from AI-optimized servers was $16.4 billion, twice the revenue a year ago. That demand led Dell to lift its fiscal 2027 revenue outlook by $25 billion to $192 billion. The company also raised its adjusted earnings guidance, to $25.50 a share from $17.90.
The quarter itself was good too. Revenue rose 58% to a record $47 billion and adjusted earnings were $7.04 per share. Revenue from traditional servers and networking also more than doubled.
The company now anticipates full-year sales from Dell AI-optimized servers to reach $74 billion, up from its earlier prediction of $60 billion.
That makes the $95 billion backlog all the more important. It indicates the AI hardware cycle is not only appearing in current sales but extending far into future quarters.

The next test is running. Investors will be scrutinizing how fast Dell can turn orders into revenue given the component shortages, while safeguarding margins, with such a massive backlog already booked.

title: Dell's AI Backlog Just Hit a Record $95 Billion
